hypothesis.title: Client requests reserved after a restart are addressed to a server the plan never crashes, split by workload seed, with a run-end census of post-restart survivor operations and redirect-insensitive acks
hypothesis.description: Plan-generation change in spur/spur-core/src/simulator/path/generator.rs, post-fault pass, under a new plan cell drawn from the workload seed exactly as recover_deps.rs draws RecoverDeps (new module survivor_target.rs: SurvivorTarget::{Stock, Survivor}, of_workload_seed(seed) = salted_phase(seed, SURVIVOR_SALT, 2) == 1, own salt so the cell is independent of the recover-deps cell). On the Survivor cell, after the stock post-fault pass has chosen its reserved client requests (recover -> request edges, unchanged), each reserved request whose target is a server that has a CrashNode stub in the plan is rewritten to a server drawn uniformly from the plan's never-crashing servers, using a SmallRng seeded from the workload seed under a second salt so the stock workload stream is byte-identical (the generator's fingerprint tests must still pass on the Stock cell). When the plan crashes every server (about 7% of plans: 3 crashes on 3 distinct servers) nothing is rewritten. Pre-fault requests, reads and writes alike, are untouched. Wiring as recover_deps: GeneratorConfig gains survivor_target: SurvivorTarget; run_single_simulation derives it from workload_seed; run_variant.rs gains POST_FAULT_SURVIVOR_TARGET = 1 << 26 joined to the tag like RECOVER_DEPS_EXEMPT (a plan-cell bit, disjoint from every id bit, inherited by replay children through the parent's seed); decide.ts row 67108864 renamed from the retired originAlternate to postFaultSurvivorTarget. Counters (util_stats.rs, new PlanShapeStats block): plan_shape.survivor.reserved_seen, plan_shape.survivor.reserved_retargeted, plan_shape.survivor.plans_without_survivor at plan time; and per cell at run end, folded from a per-run struct kept beside RunCrossingState: plan_shape.cell.{stock,survivor}.runs, .post_restart_invocations_at_survivor (client requests invoked at a target with incarnation 0 while at least two servers have incarnation > 0), .post_restart_writes_at_survivor, .post_restart_reads_at_survivor, .acked_writes_at_survivor_after_two_restarts (a write whose response arrived while the responding server had incarnation 0 and at least two servers had incarnation > 0, counted at the ClientInterface response whatever the invocation's target, so redirected writes count), .acked_writes_with_stranded_records (the same ack while the network queue held records addressed to that server from at least two distinct dead incarnations, read with state.fault_crossing as the closed write-ring signal did), .reads_invoked_after_such_ack. No config field; general_vr.json untouched.
buildsOn: recover_deps plan cell by workload seed (merged, bit 1<<13)
hypothesis.rationale: Supply read from the merged-tree cache (seed 1000, 757,560 runs): the post-fault pass reserves 2,049,069 request edges over 1,720,330 recovers (1.19 per recover), 1,578,616 requests are invoked after a run's last recover (2.08 per run), and about 3.0 client requests per run are invoked after the first crash (client_anchor.census: 1,567,477 over 521,497 treated runs, 695,726 over 236,063 control runs). Every reserved request draws its target uniformly over the servers, so a request that lands at the plan's never-crashing server after two restarts is one third of them, about 0.5 per run in the 535,949 runs (71%) with two or more recovered nodes. The oracle's label 10 is a write invoked at the never-restarted node after both restarts, and the 9-to-10 conversion is 423/2,674 = 0.158 on seed 1000 and 396/2,596 = 0.153 on seed 1001, close to the product of the reserved request being a write (about 1/3: 2-4 writes against 4-8 reads) and its target being the survivor (1/3) plus the other routes, so rung 10 reads as plan-supply-bound, not scheduler-bound. Label 13 (a read at the survivor, or at either restarted node) converts from 12 at 15/40 = 0.375 and 24/57 = 0.42. This cell removes the target factor for reserved requests only. The census separates two things the ladder confounds: the oracle matches client operations by the invocation's destination (traceanalyzer candidates.go parseInvocationPayload), while the protocol under test redirects a request at a non-leader to the leader within one round trip (ClientInterface retry loop), so a write invoked at the second-restarted node after both restarts reaches the same replication at the survivor and is not label 10, whereas one invoked at the first-restarted node after it completed its epoch change is accepted there and cannot be lost. The redirect-insensitive ack counter therefore rises less than label 10 if the rung has been measuring the invocation target rather than the state; that gap is the premise reading. Generic reading of the oracle past the write: the ladder's chain is 13 rungs long, there are no rungs 14-20; the seven off-chain DAG events are (a) the first-crashed node's restart, a predecessor of the write and so already required at depth 10, (b) the two recovery replies to the second-restarted node from the never-restarted and first-restarted nodes, predecessors of label 11 (the second-restarted node must have finished recovering before its replication ack counts), (c) the two dead-incarnation view-change records addressed to the never-restarted node, ordered AFTER label 11 as leaves the depth metric never checks, and (d) reads at the first- and second-restarted nodes as alternatives to label 13. The violating ending: a write acknowledged by the never-restarted node (still leading the old epoch) on the second-restarted node's current-incarnation ack, while the two stale view-change records addressed to it are still undelivered; the first-restarted node's completion broadcast then lands at the never-restarted node, which adopts the new epoch's log lacking the acked write; a read invoked after that at any server is routed to the first-restarted node (the new leader), replicated to the never-restarted node in the new epoch, and returns the list without the acked uid: a completed write missing from a later read. Unlabelled but required: the completion broadcast to the second-restarted node must not land before it acks the write, and no timer at the survivor or the second-restarted node moves the epoch first.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: Stated only in plan terms: a client request reserved after a restart is addressed to a server the plan never crashes. No handler, message, role, timer label or leader notion is used; the survivor is a property of the plan's own crash stubs. On any protocol the class 'client work at the node that kept its memory across the faults, issued while the restarted nodes hold ghost state' is the generic recovery-versus-client race; the stock half keeps client work at restarted nodes for bugs of the other class, and the panel's clean specs see only a different target draw on half the runs.

Labels 1-9 involve no post-fault client request, so the primary rung depth>=8 per run is expected in [0.90, 1.06]: null, with the lower edge admitting the traffic effect the grid-post-fault-2 arm shows (two random post-fault requests per restart read depth>=8 per run at 0.83x of grid on both seeds). depth>=9 [0.90, 1.10]. depth>=10 is the rung the cell feeds: the reserved write's target factor goes from 1/3 to 1, so the 9-to-10 conversion is expected to move from 0.16 to 0.25-0.40 and the per-run ratio to [1.4, 2.6]. depth>=11 carries the same lift at the fresh 10-to-11 conversion (0.14-0.17) so [1.3, 2.6]; depth>=13 [1.2, 3.5], since reserved reads also land at the survivor (r1). If the treated cell reads fewer than 10 such acks per chunk while its depth>=11 count exceeds 30, the finding is filed as 'the leaf condition (stale records undelivered at the ack) is not supplied at any target', the plan lens closes at label 11 and no rung ratio on this cell is merged as a gain.

hypothesis.redTeam: Strongest case against: label 10's target constraint is stricter than the violation's. A write invoked at the second-restarted server (still in the old epoch, not the leader) is redirected to the survivor in one round trip and produces the same replication, so it is violation-relevant but not label 10; only an invocation at the first-restarted server after its epoch change is truly lost to the ending (accepted in the new epoch). The cell therefore inflates label 10 by up to 3x (target factor 1/3 to 1) while the violation-relevant write supply moves at most 1.5x (2/3 to 1), and the ending's leaf condition - two dead-incarnation records addressed to the survivor still undelivered when it acks, hundreds of network steps after they were sent, plus the completion broadcast not yet at the restarted peer - is untouched by any target rewrite. The 15-24 depth-13 runs per chunk are all linearizable, which says the leaf, not the target, is what is missing. What separates ladder inflation from a gain: the redirect-insensitive ack counter (acked_writes_at_survivor_after_two_restarts, counted at the response whatever the invocation target) rising much less than label 10, and acked_writes_with_stranded_records reading near zero on both cells - the latter closes the plan lens at label 11 regardless of what the rungs read. A read returning a shorter list is the checker's finding, not the ladder's. Small real effect in its favor: a survivor-addressed write skips two hops, shortening the window in which the stale records can land.
hypothesis.scoreReason: Every cited figure re-derives on the fresh cache (edges 2,049,069 over 1,720,330 recovers = 1.19; 1,578,616 after the last recover = 2.08 per run; 3.01 and 2.95 after the first crash; 535,949 two-restart runs with 91,061 completing = 83.0% ending before completion; 9-to-10 0.158/0.153; 12-to-13 0.375/0.421; grid-post-fault-2 at 0.826/0.829 of grid at depth>=8 with 9-to-10 0.193/0.219 against 0.152/0.157). Targets are uniform in generate_base_actions and the post-fault pass never rewrites them. The oracle reading, the invocation-destination matcher and the redirect are verified in source. The rule is a plan-shape rule any protocol can use (a server the plan never crashes) and the stock cell is byte-identical by the recover_deps pattern. New premise against the closed post-fault-client-work family: that family varied the reservation COUNT and closed on rungs at or below 8, which no reservation can feed (labels 1-9 contain no post-fault request); this varies the reservation's TARGET on rungs 10 and 13, and the gpf2 arm on this cache already shows the reservation moving the 9-to-10 conversion. The census reads the leaf condition the ladder is blind to, which is the premise check the lens asks for. Power: about 210 depth-10 events per half per chunk resolve the 1.4x lower edge on one chunk. Docked from 8 because the violation-relevant gain is bounded near 1.5x by the proposer's own redirect argument.

pairedHypothesis.title: The request reserved after a restart is a write when one is available and one read is pulled behind it so the read's invocation follows the write's response, split by workload seed
pairedHypothesis.description: Plan-generation change in generator.rs, post-fault pass, under a plan cell drawn from the workload seed (new module post_fault_shape.rs: PostFaultShape::{Stock, WriteThenRead}, own salt). On the WriteThenRead cell, for each recover the candidate list is the stock shuffled list filtered to write-like requests (Write or Rmw) not path-connected with the recover; if it is non-empty the first is taken and the edge recover -> write is added as today (one reserved request per recover, post_fault_client_ops unchanged); if it is empty the stock choice is made (counted as a fallback). Then one read not path-connected with that write, preferring reads not already reserved after any recover, gets the mandatory edge write -> read, so the read becomes ready only when the write's response completes the plan event (path.rs marks the plan event complete on the response). The read is one of the plan's existing reads pulled from the run's start to after the write, so the number of client requests is unchanged; the second pass's probabilistic edges and the cycle guard see the graph with these edges present, exactly as the write-chain edges are treated. Stock cell byte-identical (fingerprint tests). Wiring as recover_deps: GeneratorConfig.post_fault_shape, derived in run_single_simulation from workload_seed; run_variant.rs POST_FAULT_WRITE_THEN_READ = 1 << 29 joined as a plan-cell bit; decide.ts row 536870912 renamed from the retired pairOrderGhostOnly to postFaultWriteThenRead. Counters (PlanShapeStats): plan_shape.write_read.pairs_added, .write_fallbacks (no write available), .read_unavailable (write reserved, no read free), at plan time; per cell at run end: plan_shape.cell.{stock,write_then_read}.runs, .post_restart_writes_invoked (writes invoked while at least two servers have incarnation > 0), .post_restart_write_acks, .reads_invoked_after_post_restart_write_ack (reads whose invocation step follows the response step of such a write), .reads_invoked_after_survivor_state_moved_post_ack (such a read invoked after the responding server, at incarnation 0, took a state-changing delivery from a restarted peer's current incarnation following the ack), .acked_writes_with_stranded_records and .reads_invoked_after_such_ack as in the survivor cell. No config field; general_vr.json untouched.

generator.rs post-fault pass and write-chain pass
path.rs plan completion on client response
pairedHypothesis.rationale: Two plan facts read from the generator and the cache. First, the stock reservation draws its request uniformly over all client requests, so it is a write about one third of the time (2-4 writes against 4-8 reads); label 10 needs a write after both restarts, and the 9-to-10 conversion is 0.158 and 0.153 on the two seeds. Second, nothing in a stock plan orders a read after a post-fault write: reads not reserved are all ready at step 0 and issued at once (path.rs get_ready_events), a reserved read becomes ready at its recover, i.e. at the same step as a write reserved after the same recover, so the two are concurrent and a read concurrent with the write may legally return the old value; only the density-0.3 half (334,669 of 757,560 runs) supplies write -> read edges by chance, at about 0.15 per (write, read) pair. The ending needs a read invoked after the write's response (and after the completion broadcast lands): the 12-to-13 conversion is 0.375 and 0.42, and 12 to 13 is the rung whose event is a plan event, so it is the cleanest supply-bound rung in the ladder. This cell makes the reserved request a write and pulls one read behind its response on every restart, changing the count of client requests by zero. The blocked fault-frontier-client-reservation entry proposed a state-mutating preference; this differs in keeping per-restart reservation and in adding the dependent read, which is the event class label 13 needs, and it answers the block: the zero ablation of post_fault_client_ops measured rungs at or below 8 on a tree with no events at labels 10-13, and those are the only rungs a reserved request can feed; on this cache they read 423, 59, 40 and 15 per chunk, so that null bounds nothing here. Traffic risk from the cache: the grid-post-fault-2 arm (two random post-fault requests per restart) reads depth>=8 per run at 0.83x of grid on both seeds while its 9-to-10 conversion reads 0.19 and 0.22 against 0.15 and 0.16, so more post-fault client work costs the ghost chain and pays at the write; this cell adds no request and moves one read later, so the depth-8 cost is expected smaller. Generic reading of the oracle past the write: the ladder's chain is 13 rungs long, there are no rungs 14-20; the seven off-chain DAG events are (a) the first-crashed node's restart, a predecessor of the write and so already required at depth 10, (b) the two recovery replies to the second-restarted node from the never-restarted and first-restarted nodes, predecessors of label 11 (the second-restarted node must have finished recovering before its replication ack counts), (c) the two dead-incarnation view-change records addressed to the never-restarted node, ordered AFTER label 11 as leaves the depth metric never checks, and (d) reads at the first- and second-restarted nodes as alternatives to label 13. The violating ending: a write acknowledged by the never-restarted node (still leading the old epoch) on the second-restarted node's current-incarnation ack, while the two stale view-change records addressed to it are still undelivered; the first-restarted node's completion broadcast then lands at the never-restarted node, which adopts the new epoch's log lacking the acked write; a read invoked after that at any server is routed to the first-restarted node (the new leader), replicated to the never-restarted node in the new epoch, and returns the list without the acked uid: a completed write missing from a later read. Unlabelled but required: the completion broadcast to the second-restarted node must not land before it acks the write, and no timer at the survivor or the second-restarted node moves the epoch first.
pairedHypothesis.generalityArgument: A plan-shape rule only: after a restart the reserved client work is a state-mutating request followed by a read that starts after it completes. It names no handler, message or role; it is the generic 'write then read across a fault boundary' probe every linearizability checker wants, since a read that starts after a write's response is the only read that can witness a lost write. Protocols without restarts see no change (no recover stubs); the stock half keeps the uniform reservation.

depth13Band.note: a lean only; the pulled read is label 13 only when the broadcast lands inside the ack-to-response window

pairedHypothesis.redTeam: Three cases against. (i) The depth-13 mechanism rests on a wrong ordering claim: label 13 is a read INVOKED after label 12 (the completion broadcast landing at the survivor); the pulled read is invoked at the write's response, and the broadcast lands at the survivor at a later network step, so the pulled read counts as label 13 only when the broadcast lands between the replication reply and the response's delivery. The read can still witness the violation - a read logged at the survivor in the old epoch is redirected when the broadcast installs the new epoch (enter_normal_mode redirects pending requests) - but only if the broadcast lands within that read's two replication hops, the same delivery-order race the leaf needs; the ladder does not count it. (ii) As written the cell cannibalizes the ladder's root: with 2-4 writes and 1-3 recovers, reserving a write at every recover leaves no unreserved write on plans with writes <= recovers ((2,2),(2,3),(3,3)) - one third of all plans and one half of the plans with two or more recovers - and on those a write at the survivor before the timer and the first crash is impossible, so the run reads depth 0 whatever follows. The depth>=8 band [0.88, 1.06] and the 'close' falsifier would fire by construction for a reason the violation does not share (the violating path needs no pre-fault write). (iii) Rung 10's write factor is real, but a write reserved after the FIRST-executed recover is invoked before the second restart and is not label 10; only the later recover's reservation can be. What separates inflation from gain: the outstanding-read counter added below (a read unanswered at the survivor when its state moved after the ack) and the per-cell 9-to-10 conversion, not the raw rung.

reviewSummary: Fourteen candidates scored blind against the fresh merged-tree cache (63a21f95fdfb, seeds 1000/1001), the oracle DAG, the matcher and the source. Oracle reading verified: the root-anchored chain is 13 rungs (w1 ... deliver_pok_2_to_0, deliver_sv_1_to_0, r1|r2|r3), no rungs 14-20; the seven off-chain events are recover_nl (also a predecessor of label 7, so required from depth 7 - the proposals say depth 10), the two recovery replies (predecessors of label 11), the two stale view-change records to the survivor (leaves after label 11, never checked by rootAnchoredPrefix) and r2/r3 (alternatives to r1). The matcher keys client labels on the invocation's destination (candidates.go collectClientInvocations) while VR.spur redirects to the leader in one round trip, so label 10 is stricter than the violation (an invocation at the second-restarted node reaches the same replication). The ending verified in generic terms, with one addition: enter_normal_mode redirects every pending request, so a read logged at the survivor in the old epoch and overtaken by the completion broadcast is also a witness, which is wider than label 13. Ranking: survivor target 7, write-then-read 6 (with a design constraint), repeated release 5, read train 4, backlog 4, run-local counters 3 net (5-2), pre-fault root probe 3, defer coin 3, PCT 3, stalled parents 2, post-release cap 2, cover-edge 2. Rejected: state fork and gen-2 admission as parentless (the ring closed at iteration 83; the fork's cut-depth premise is refuted by the ring's mean cut step 315). Post-fault family: the survivor cell stands first (every supply figure verified; its census reads the leaf condition the ladder is blind to), write-then-read pairs with it in one two-bit session (independent workload-seed salts, 2x2 crossed cells, replay and AOS children inherit the plan), the read train waits as the third bit. None re-admits the closed count family without a new premise: that family closed on rungs at or below 8, which no reservation can feed, and this cache's gpf2 arm shows the reservation moving the 9-to-10 conversion; the new cells vary target and type on rungs 10 and 13 and add a census of the ack-with-stranded-records condition. False checkable claims: write-then-read's 12-to-13 mechanism (the pulled read is invoked at the ack, before the broadcast lands at the survivor, so it is not label 13 on most runs) and its unstated root cannibalization (a write at every recover leaves no pre-fault write on half the two-restart plans); the pre-fault probe's depth>=1 rise to 0.80-0.92 (false by symmetry; the lift is conditional on sole-survivor plans and appears from depth>=5); stalled parents' 352,842 (267,533, fourth round); PCT's handful of timer wakes (153 per run); run-local counters' absolute values (previous cache; identity holds). Meta probe: it is a plan-shape experiment and could ride as a second bit, but its label (1) is one the violation does not need and its root factor is arithmetic (about 1.46); it does not displace write-then-read. Recommended session: postFaultSurvivorTarget = 1<<26 (row 67108864, originAlternate renamed) and postFaultWriteThenRead = 1<<29 (row 536870912, pairOrderGhostOnly renamed) with the last-free-write guard; primary depth>=8 null on both, advance reads on depth>=10/11 and the per-cell 9-to-10 conversion; the decisive premise read is acked_writes_with_stranded_records per cell (near zero on both closes the plan lens at label 11). Bit conflicts resolved: repeated release takes 1<<25 or the next free row when it leads; backlog and PCT wait; 1<<22 is available to the pre-fault probe only in a session that does not build the deep-supply walk.

The train's first read is the parent's (invoked at the ack, before the broadcast lands); later reads follow only after each response, so the train samples the post-ack window once per replication round, and whether the broadcast lands during the train is the same delivery-order race the leaf needs.
